summary: The study investigates the influence of composition within multilayered heterostructure oxide semiconductors on the performance of thin-film transistors (TFTs). The heterostructures, comprising alternating polycrystalline indium oxide and zinc oxide layers, are fabricated using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The process allows for tuning of electrical properties by controlling the thickness of individual layers, resulting in enhanced TFT performance after mild thermal annealing at 200 °C. The study demonstrates superior transistor characteristics, including an average field-effect mobility of 9.3 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, an on/off ratio of 5.3 × 10⁹, and a subthreshold swing of 162 mV dec⁻¹, along with excellent long-term and bias stress stability. The findings highlight the potential of ALD-based heterostructure oxides for low-temperature TFT applications.

This subsequently results in enhanced TFT performance for the optimized stacked architecture after mild thermal annealing at temperatures as low as 200 °C.'
